trace: The plan involves exploiting the phenomenon where small-cap stocks with high liquidity often exhibit outperformance due to their ability to absorb trading without significantly affecting price. This effect is believed to persist because market participants tend to favor these stocks for both strategic and regulatory reasons, leading to higher liquidity and lower bid-ask spreads. The rule would be to screen for the most liquid equities within a small-cap segment, then construct an equal-weighted portfolio of these screened stocks. This approach aims to capture the benefits of increased liquidity while maintaining diversification across numerous firms.

The signal for this strategy involves ranking stocks based on their liquidity metrics. Specifically, compute the average daily trading volume over a 30-day lookback period. Higher average volumes indicate greater liquidity. On a given day, rank all small-cap equities by their 30-day average trading volume in descending order. Select the top-n most liquid stocks (e.g., based on historical testing) to construct an equal-weighted portfolio. This ranking ensures that the most liquid stocks are prioritized for inclusion, leveraging the observed outperformance of highly traded small-cap stocks due to lower bid-ask spreads and greater market participation.

This strategy involves holding a portfolio of up to 30 most liquid small-cap stocks, equally weighted at 3.33% each. Position sizes are equalized to maintain diversification while leveraging liquidity benefits. Risk limits are set to ensure that any single stock does not contribute more than 3.33% to the overall portfolio risk, thereby bounding potential loss from individual stock underperformance to a minimum level.
